linked_work.title: Couldn't obtain version info from github: Network error

judgment.rationale: The current archive shows historical GitHub update-check network failures, but the issue body still does not say what visible problem occurred, and a closely matching earlier issue was resolved as a machine NIC/connectivity problem rather than a PowerToys code defect.
evidence: The issue body contains only a diagnostic ZIP and leaves steps to reproduce plus expected/actual behavior blank.
Runner logs in the attached archive repeatedly record `Couldn't obtain version info from github: Network error` across many startup sessions from 2026-07-17 through 2026-08-30.
A later log in the same archive (`RunnerLogs/runner-log_2026-09-06.log`) records `Version is up to date`, so the updater path was not failing continuously in every session.

There is no assignee, linked PR, or maintainer comment beyond the automated request for reproduction details.
judgment.recommended_action: Request the exact visible updater failure and same-machine connectivity state, then keep the issue waiting on author evidence instead of starting a speculative fix design.

fix_assessment.rationale: A PowerToys code fix is not actionable from the current evidence because the archive is consistent with intermittent external connectivity failure and the reporter has not yet described a reproducible user-facing defect.

issue_context.summary: The report is currently a bare diagnostic upload. The attached Runner logs show repeated failures while contacting GitHub for version information, but the issue does not yet say whether the reporter saw a Settings error, a startup notification, or only noticed the log entry.
known_information: The issue was filed on 2026-09-09 against PowerToys v0.101.2362 from the Microsoft Store.
The issue area is General, there is no assignee, and the issue is labeled Needs-Author-Feedback after the automated triage comment.

inferences: The current evidence more strongly suggests intermittent GitHub reachability or local network filtering than a deterministic PowerToys logic bug.
Because the archive also shows at least one later successful check, the missing discriminator is the visible failure mode and surrounding network state, not another blind request for generic logs.
If the reporter only noticed the historical log entry and did not see an actual update symptom, the issue may not need code work at all.
issue_context.analysis: Focused investigation found a plausible explanation before asking for more evidence: the same error string is emitted only when GitHub version lookup fails, the archive shows repeated failures but at least one later success, and the closest upstream duplicate was resolved as a host-network problem. That means the next maintainer question should not be another generic bug-report request. The missing facts are the exact visible symptom, whether GitHub and Store connectivity fail at the same time, and whether a VPN/proxy/firewall layer is involved.

comment.body:
Thanks for attaching the report bundle. It already shows repeated Runner update-check failures (Couldn't obtain version info from github: Network error) across older sessions, but the issue form still does not say what visible problem you hit. The same error signature in #29515 turned out to be a machine connectivity/NIC issue, and your archive also shows at least one later successful update check.

Please provide:
1. The exact action and visible result now: for example, whether **Settings > Check for updates** shows a network error, whether you saw a startup/update notification, or whether you only noticed the log entry.
2. Whether github.com, the PowerToys releases page, and Microsoft Store are reachable from the same machine when this happens.
3. Whether a VPN, proxy, firewall, or security/network-filtering product is active, and whether disabling only that layer changes the behavior.

This will distinguish a reproducible PowerToys updater bug from the external connectivity pattern previously seen in #29515.
